messages:
maria: heads-up, ~180 tiny-gpu pods are Pending in us-west2 this morning, causing p95 spikes on inference routes :eyes:

sam: saw that too. kubectl describe shows a lot of "0/15 nodes are available: 15 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu" but several nodes show idle resources in the node list.

leo: I think it's a GPU flavor mismatch. last week's scale-up added A100-80GB nodes (full GPUs) and we still have A10/MIG nodes. scheduler is treating gpu resources as homogeneous, so MIG-sliced tiny pods are constrained by nodeSelector/gpu.type=mig. full nodes are effectively wasted for these tiny slices.

anya: that matches the cost dashboard — we intentionally scaled full-GPU pool for batch, but warm-pool contains the MIG workload. Keeping both pools is burning $$ and fragmenting capacity.

sam: paste of scheduling trace from a pending pod:
```
I0226 09:12:43 predicateChecker.go:189] Fit failed for pod tiny-infer-abc: PodRejectReason: node doesn't have matching label: gpu.type=mig
I0226 09:12:43 predicateChecker.go:190] Node candidate pool-full-3: resources OK but label mismatch
```

maria: so pods are waiting on a label match even though a full node could run them if we provisioned MIG slices at runtime. can we have a graceful fallback?

leo: short-term ops options:
- relax nodeSelector on tiny-gpu pods -> faster placement but risk landing latency-sensitive slices on oversized hardware (and harder isolation)
- implement nodeLabelMapping + scheduler predicate to let full nodes accept MIG workloads by enabling dynamic MIG provisioning (needs driver+kubelet changes and a maintenance window)

anya: cost tradeoffs: relaxing selector will reduce queue p95 by ~200ms but could increase run cost since full nodes are pricier. dynamic-MIG provisioning has an upfront ops cost but cleaner long-term and reduces wasted capacity.

sam: immediate mitigation I can try: tweak Karpenter / GKE autoscaler profile to bias new tiny-gpu pods to the MIG nodegroup and kick a small scale-up (minDelta=3) for us-west2b, then drain 2-3 nodes from full-pool and reimage with MIG-capable driver as a canary.

maria: do canary in us-west2b only, add autoscaler safety cap, and ping infra oncall.

scheduler-bot: [autoscaler] scaleUp request queued for nodegroup-mig-pool-us-west2b (minDelta=3) — triggered by pending pods: tiny-infer-* :hourglass_flowing_sand:

anya: I'll notify finance. rough estimate if we convert 6 nodes to MIG config: +$2.4k/month (net of reduced batch-use savings) — sending modeling to infra-costs@.

leo: follow-up: we should add an admission/scheduler policy that prefers gpu.family compatibility before requiring exact node labels; basically a compatibility matrix so full nodes can be considered for MIG slices where possible. I'll draft a short RFC after the canary.

maria: sounds good. @sam post the canary playbook and start time here when scheduled. :thumbsup:

sam: will do. aiming for canary start 09:30 PT — playbook will include rollback steps, autoscaler cap, and metrics to watch (pending count, p95 latency, cost burn-rate).

maria: thanks. keeping this thread for updates only.
